source_vocabularies.opp115_category: ml/data/opp115_schema.py CATEGORIES (10 values, verified against the released corpus)
source_vocabularies.opp115_data_type: the 'Personal Information Type' attribute, 17 distinct values measured across all 115 annotated policies on 2026-11-06

principles: Only the two OPP-115 categories that describe data being collected or shared can name a Data Safety category. The other eight describe practices *about* data - choice, access, retention, security, policy change, Do Not Track, specific audiences, other - and a Data Safety category is a statement about what data is handled, not about how it is governed. Mapping 'Data Security' to a data category would report a security promise as a collection declaration.

A rule is keyed on the data type, because the Data Safety taxonomy is a taxonomy of data. An OPP-115 category alone never names one: 'First Party Collection/Use' says the first party collects something, not what.

is_partial marks a correspondence that is real but looser than one-to-one, either because the OPP-115 value is broader than the Data Safety category or because it spans more than one. A partial mapping is still evidence; it is flagged so a report can say how tight the correspondence was.

A value with no defensible counterpart is left out and listed under unmapped_data_types with the reason. An absent rule produces no mapped practice, which is the correct outcome: silence, not a guess.

rules.rationale: Both names denote the user's geographic position. Data Safety's Location covers approximate and precise location; OPP-115 does not distinguish them, which does not affect the category.

OPP-115 'Contact' is the user's own contact details - name, email, postal address, phone. Data Safety places those under Personal info. It is NOT Data Safety 'Contacts', which is the user's address book, i.e. other people's details. The two names are near-homographs for different things and conflating them would be the single easiest error in this table.
Payment details, purchase history and credit information in both taxonomies.
Health information in both. Data Safety splits health from fitness within one category, which OPP-115 does not, and the split does not change the mapping.
Age, gender, race and similar attributes. Data Safety lists race, ethnicity, political or religious beliefs, sexual orientation and other user characteristics under Personal info.
Data Safety's Personal info includes 'User IDs' and other identifiers attached to a person. Distinct from Device or other IDs, which identifies hardware or an installation rather than a person.
Data Safety's Device or other IDs names device identifiers, advertising identifiers and IP-derived identifiers explicitly.

Cookies and pixels function as identifiers tied to a browser or installation, which is what Device or other IDs covers. Partial: a cookie may also carry session state that is not an identifier, and OPP-115 does not separate the two.

Browser type, operating system and hardware attributes. Partial, and deliberately so: Data Safety has no category for non-identifying device characteristics, and this OPP-115 value conflates attributes used for identification with attributes used for compatibility. The flag records that the correspondence is one-directional.

In-application actions, searches and interaction history. Partial because this OPP-115 value also covers activity outside the application, which Data Safety separates into Web browsing; both rules are present and a practice of this type maps to both.

The second half of the same split. Data Safety's Web browsing is browsing history outside the application. Emitting both and flagging each partial is more honest than silently choosing one, because the source value genuinely does not distinguish them.
The annotator recorded personal information without naming a kind. Partial: the correspondence holds at the level of 'this is personal information' and nowhere narrower.
Account profile attributes. Partial: a profile aggregates several Data Safety categories and the value does not say which are present.

The same value with the capitalisation the corpus also uses. Both spellings occur in the released annotations (216 and 112 occurrences), so both are listed rather than normalised: normalising here would hide a corpus fact from anyone reading this table against the data.
Profile and activity imported from a social network. Partial: it may also carry Contacts or Photos and videos, which this value does not distinguish.
The data type is the same; the sharing dimension is carried separately by the declaration's is_shared flag and is not part of this mapping.
As for first-party Contact: the user's own contact details, which Data Safety places under Personal info.

unmapped_data_types.reason: The annotator recorded that no data type was identifiable. It is the corpus's explicit 'nothing to select' value. Mapping the commonest value in the attribute to any Data Safety category would manufacture a declaration out of an annotator's abstention, and it would do so 4,299 times.
A residual bucket with no shared meaning across its members. Any single Data Safety category would be wrong for most of them.
Data Safety has no survey category. Survey responses may contain anything from demographics to health, and the value does not say which, so there is no category this can be asserted to be.

unmapped_categories.reason: Describes the control a user has over data, not which data is handled. Opt-out language is not a collection declaration.
Describes access and deletion rights, not categories of data collected.
Describes how long data is kept. A retention period is a property of a practice, not a data category.

Describes protection measures. Reporting a security promise as a Data Safety category would turn 'we encrypt your data' into a declaration that the data is collected, which is a different claim and, in a consistency audit, a damaging one.
Describes how the policy itself is amended.
Describes the response to a browser signal.
Describes jurisdiction and audience, such as children or EU residents, not data categories.
Residual bucket, by definition without a specific meaning to map.
